_doc: Loose cultivators (tán tu) of regions 10-20: tier A, tier B and the dead. Tier C in loose-south.2.cast.json. Page: loose-south.md.

people.gloss: White-headed one of the mound (bạch thủ is also 'empty-handed')
people.role: The ruin-digger of Vô Định Thành and the only man who has walked the miasma of Chiết Kích Nguyên and come out (age 310)
people.appearance: Snow-white hair since he was ten, a brown unlined face, and a goat bell on a cord at his wrist that he silences with his thumb when he talks.
people.backstory: In 900 a herder's boy of Thụ Âm Thôn followed his goat into the miasma on the Pivot's side of the plain and walked out three days later, grey-haired and calm (A214). Quý Thủ Lũy (quy_thu_luy), who keeps the barrow watch, was the one who found him at the edge and asked what he had seen. He said grass. At thirty he crossed to the Lạc Hà side and began to dig the ash of Vô Định Thành, which burned in 803 (C158), and he has dug it for 280 years. He sells what he finds at Thiên Bảo Trai's season auction, and Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa) knows his lots by their smell. The Miasma Watch turns back every treasure seeker except him, and Mông Thiết Sơn (mong_thiet_son) has buried forty who would not take his advice. He lives in Tân Khẩu Thôn, the refugees' harbour where no one speaks of the plain (A182), and he is the one man there who does, plainly, about anything but those three days. When Hình Lạc Nhạn (hinh_lac_nhan) was a child at the Watch he taught her which grey moves and which does not. He sells Giản Vạn Lộ (gian_van_lo) a map of the plain every spring, and every one is wrong.
people.wants: To sell the plain once: one true map of the safe ways, to a buyer strong enough that he lives through the sale, for enough to die rich in Tân Khẩu.
people.secret: In 900 he reached the middle of the plain. The grey rises from carved stones laid in rings under the soil, and each stone bears a sunset cloud: Lạc Hà's founder's seal. He has known for three hundred years that the miasma was laid, and by whom, and that ten thousand of his friend's dead are Lạc Hà's work. In the ring nearest the old river road a blue sword lay where it had been dropped, among the bones, and he did not touch it.

tree.targets_note: Earthen Gate and Blessed Basin for health, Battlements and Array Keeper for wards, Steady Steps and Warding Stone for resistance to what is in the air (wish W5-earth-poison-resist).

people.gloss: The fierce lady of the Đồ
people.role: Mistress of the bandit camp at Thạch Môn Trại on the Pivot road; the last of the Hắc Phong rogues (age 295)
people.appearance: Tall and heavy-shouldered, her left forearm a lacework of lightning scars, a hooked blade at each hip and one of them always clean.
people.backstory: Đồ Liệt Cơ was born in 905 in Hắc Phong Trại, the stockade whose rogue cultivators robbed the ore trains of Ngọc Hành for sixty years. Her father Đồ Thiết Hống (do_thiet_hong) ran it. In 940 Thiên Xu cleared it (V126). Her father died at the gate, and she went over the north wall on a rope with eleven others while the stockade burned. Her little brother Đồ Vô Cữu (do_vo_cuu), twenty, was taken, spared for his age and kept as a hunter (N-thien_xu-07). She went south over the border, where the Pivot's writ does not run, and in 951 took the empty fort of Thạch Môn Trại, Khải Lôi's old garrison that the Tower let go in 645 (V155). For 250 years her camp has robbed the Pivot's ore buyers and the southern caravans on the road to the Night Rain Market. It has never touched a Tower train, and since the Night Rain Market opened in 1000 (C198) it has paid the market a tithe through Kiều Mãn Lâu (kieu_man_lau). The Tower lets it stand, because a bandit camp on the Pivot road is a wall it does not have to man. Her brother hunts rogues for the Pivot and has never once come south. She knows he could find her in a month, and that he let a stockade boy go twice in the north.
people.wants: A Thunder-rooted heir for the camp before her lifespan turns (she has her eye on Bành Tiểu Điện), and one meeting with her brother before one of them dies.
people.secret: Twelve went over the wall in 940, not eleven. The twelfth was still on the rope when the Pivot's archers reached the wall, and the eleven below would have died with him. She cut it. He was her brother. He fell back inside, and that is why he lived.

tree.targets_note: The Twin Thunder idea for Thunder strikes, the Tempered by Lightning idea (Struck Bones, Tempered by Lightning) for a body that takes arrows, Hook Swords in the Metal land for the hooked blade.

people.role: Ferryman of the free crossing at Thủy Khẩu on the Ngư Ca border; carried the Đào Sa raiders over in 1173
people.appearance: A narrow brown man in a split straw hat, his palms grooved by the pole, a stern lamp lit on his boat in daylight.
people.backstory: Yến Hồi Độ was born in Vãn Đăng Thôn, where the fishers light their stern lamps on the dusk of 803 and do not put out (V104). He poled for Lãng Đào's boats at the Ngư Ca landing as a hired man, never sworn, and learned their pole primer. In 1162 he was told to charge Lạc Hà's boats a new toll and asked who had set it. He was let go, took his own boat down to Thủy Khẩu (A196) and kept a ferry there. In 1173 a Lạc Hà party paid him triple to carry crates across by night, in a loose man's boat so that no Boat Hall hull was seen crossing. The crates carried Nam Phố's cloud stamp, and the slip read 'for the reed beds at Thủy Khẩu'. A month later the boats he had poled beside burned at Đào Sa (A080). In 1174 Tùng Đào cut the rope bridges (A202). He saw Lô Tiểu Ca (lo_tieu_ca) fall from the last one and could not reach her. Downstream he pulled Ngô Bất Tán (ngo_bat_tan) out of the river with his leg broken in three places. His crossing has charged no fare since. He has never said what he carried.
people.wants: To tell the whole of the Ferry War once, both halves of it, to someone who will make it count, before the war is fought again.
people.secret: He kept the slip. It is in Kha Triêu Phi's (kha_trieu_phi) hand. He also knows the toll that started the war was never set by the pines: Giang Cửu Khúc (giang_cuu_khuc) set it, and Yến was the first man told to collect it.

tree.intent: Wood and Water sustain and wards: a boat that does not sink and a man who does not tire.
tree.targets_note: Seedling and Spirit Spring for Wood sustain, Water Wears Stone and Nourishing Rain for Water's, Ice Mirror's ward: a boat that does not sink.

people.role: Seller of maps at the Night Rain Market in Thu Trì; a Nam Phố scribe turned out in 1168
people.appearance: A soft-spoken man with ink to the second knuckle, eyes that do not narrow in the dark, and a rolled map behind each ear.
people.backstory: Giản Vạn Lộ was born in 1132 in Hầu Đầu Thôn, a mushroom-pickers' village on the karst, and as a boy he could see in the caves as if it were noon. He told no one why, and the hall never tested for it. Đới Huyền Nghiên (doi_huyen_nghien) was the boy next door. He entered Nam Phố Đường on his Wood in 1146 and became its best copyist of maps and contracts. In 1168 Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van) turned him out for selling unstamped talismans at Hạc Đinh Thị. The hall said greed, and it was right. He walked south to Thu Trì, where the innkeepers ask no names (A313), and since 1170 he has sold maps in the Night Rain Market (A315): to Khải Lôi's sealed drum, to the dead masters' abodes, to the temple that showed on Thanh Ải Phong for a day in 1180 (A233). Nine in ten are false. He prices them all the same and never says which. Once a year he goes back into the karst under Hãm Thạch Trấn (V105) and draws what is really there. Đới still writes to him. The fortune-teller Đoan Mộc Thính (doan_moc_thinh) sings the treasure; he sells the road.
people.wants: Khâu Bạch Thủ's true map of Chiết Kích Nguyên, and one find under his own name that Nam Phố will have to hear about.
people.secret: One of the three mountains to which Triệu Huyết Y has narrowed her master's abode is one he invented and sold her in 1171, with the False Cloud Seal on the map. She means to climb it, and he has seen what she does to a seller who lied.

people.role: Fortune-teller of Thiều Âm Thị and, in the rains, of the Night Rain Market; never wrong about the weather
people.appearance: A round, cheerful woman who tilts her head before she answers, as if the wind had told her first.
people.backstory: A miner's daughter from the drill-mine of Tập Trận Khoáng, where the wind never stops. Wind woke in her at nine. She passed the Pivot's outer gate on her Earth and failed the Level Beam on a Metal of thirty, and the Pivot had no use for a root it could not weigh, so she went down to the music market below the old palace. She tells fortunes there and, in the rains, at the Night Rain Market beside Giản Vạn Lộ (gian_van_lo). She is right about the weather a day ahead every time, so people believe the rest. Her Wind carries sound to her from a day's flight off, and twice it has brought her a flute from the ridge of Kích Khánh Đường. She knows whose it is.

people.gloss: Lộc who does not go back
people.role: Sell-sword who guards buyers out of the Night Rain Market; a Pivot deserter of the Cinnabar Vein War
people.appearance: Grey at the temples, a Pivot sword with the Dipper filed off its guard, and a way of standing with his back to a wall.
people.backstory: A Pivot inner disciple from the steppe, he marched on Phượng Minh's side in the Cinnabar Vein War (C189). At the pass of Đan Sơn Mạch in 1156 he held one node of the array that closed on Kỷ Vãn Tình's rear guard (N-thinh_vu-08). He let it slip for as long as it took four of her people to carry the wounded out. Then he walked away from the Pivot. Đồ Vô Cữu (do_vo_cuu) has hunted him for forty years, and he lives where the Pivot's writ does not run.

people.gloss: The late-born daughter of the Sầm
people.role: Hunter's widow of Ô Diêu Thôn, raising a Thunder-rooted daughter that the Tower and a bandit camp both want
people.appearance: A potter's daughter's thick wrists, a hunter's knife she does not need, and clay always under one thumbnail.
people.backstory: A potter's daughter of Ô Diêu, she married the hunter Bành Liệp Hổ (banh_liep_ho) and bore their daughter in a lightning storm at the mine camp of Tử Tinh Khoáng in 1183. In 1195 the tiger-kind of Phục Hổ Cương, which took Thanh Thạch Bảo in 1041 (V160), killed her husband. The Tower's Thunder Hall has come for the girl twice. She has seen what a life lamp is for, and she would sooner give her daughter to the bandits on the road, which she will not do either.

Her mother keeps her from the Tower. At the apricot market of Hạnh Hoa Thị she met Đồ Liệt Cơ (do_liet_co), who showed her how to hold a spark in her teeth, and her mother does not know.

people.role: Spirit-beast hunter of the Kinh Trập ridge; hunts the tiger king of Phục Hổ Cương
people.appearance: A broad, slow man missing two fingers of his left hand, a tiger-whisker charm at his throat and a grey hound that never barks.
people.backstory: Born among the cave hunters of Thủ Động Trại, who keep their own order on Kinh Trập day (V152), he left the cave watch for the beast trails and is a cousin of Ôn Tịch Nhai (on_tich_nhai). He hunted the tiger-kind of Phục Hổ Cương with his sworn brother Bành Liệp Hổ (banh_liep_ho) for forty years and carried his body down in 1195. He sells cores at the Night Rain Market and pays Đồ Liệt Cơ's camp for the road. He has hunted the tiger king alone since.

people.role: Smuggler of the unlit sails: carries the Night Rain Market's goods down the gulf and pearls back north
people.appearance: Salt-cracked lips, a sailor's squint, and a coat dyed black with mangrove bark so that she is a shadow on the deck.
people.backstory: A reed-cutter's daughter of Lô Châu, the village Thôn Hải carried off in 765 (A306). A woman of her line came home from the pirates' hold in 782 (A307) knowing how they sailed with no lamp, and the family kept it as a fishers' trick. Biện runs two unlit boats out of burned Hải Diêm Trấn (V139): pearls north to the Night Rain Market, and since last winter, when Kiều Mãn Lâu (kieu_man_lau) found buyers in Phượng Minh's ports, poisons and pills south past the northern fort. On that run she steers by the one lamp on the coast that never goes out, Kiển Mục Hải's (kien_muc_hai) at Liệu Phàm Bảo.

people.role: Wreck-diver of Bích Không Cảng, the empty harbour of Cô Phàm Các; his father sailed on the first lost boat
people.appearance: Long-limbed and hollow-chested from diving, ears scarred by the deep, a Cô Phàm bronze sail-ring on his thumb.
people.backstory: His father Uông Viễn Lãng (uong_vien_lang) signed onto the first deep-water boat Lận Viễn Phàm paid for in 1158 (N-binh_thuy-05), and it was not seen again. He was eight. He lives alone on the empty quays of Bích Không Cảng (A150) and dives the reefs where Cô Phàm's charts stop. He sold Lận the bronze sail-ring's twin and kept this one. He means to be on the third boat Hầu Bách Chu (hau_bach_chu) has built and told no one about.

people.role: The musician of Thiều Âm Thị (A248): believed sent across the gulf in 1195, kept at Kích Khánh Đường
people.appearance: Thin, with a flute-player's calluses and the habit of stopping mid-word when a bird sings.
people.backstory: Chúc Hiểu Nghi's (chuc_hieu_nghi) elder brother, a flute seller's son who never sat a gate. In 1195 he played a tune no one had taught him in the market, and every bird on the ridge fell silent (A248). The elders paid his passage away. Lộ Văn Khánh (lo_van_khanh) kept him instead in the ruined chime hall of Kích Khánh Đường, where the broken chimes ring when stepped on (V133). He believes he is hidden for his own safety and that his sister is told he is well. He plays every night, and Lộ writes it down.
